I am 32, been farming 10 years on our 18 mu. My man helps with the heavy work and my mother-in-law watches the children. I went to primary school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and figure out what my neighbors are doing.

Here is how I think about this year:

**Wheat and maize** take most of my land — about 12 mu. This is how everyone here farms, one after the other, wheat in winter and maize in summer. I plant improved wheat seed from the dealer in the county town — the old seed my mother-in-law used gives less. For wheat I spread about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (那个50斤的袋子) at planting, then top-dress urea in spring when it turns green. That comes out to around 20 kg of nitrogen per mu. I water 3 times — before winter, green-up, and heading. Pesticide twice for aphids and the rust. Last year I got about 480 kg, so I aim similar.

For maize I do not plough, just no-till seed right after wheat harvest — saves time and water. Hybrid seed, one bag compound at sowing plus urea at big trumpet stage. Around 18 kg N. One irrigation if the rains are short. Spray once for borer. I got 550 kg last year.

**Cabbage** on 2 mu — this is my cash crop, sells at the county market. It eats a lot of fertilizer and water. I put manure from the village plus compound fertilizer, and water many times. Spray 4-5 times because the worms are terrible.

**Eggplant** on 2 mu — also for market. Same idea, heavy feeding, much water.

**Stevia** on 2 mu — the company gives us the seedlings and buys back the leaves. They told us not too much nitrogen or the sweetness drops. I follow what they say.

Every yuan of fertilizer matters. Four mouths to feed. I do not skimp on wheat and maize fertilizer — better waste a little than lose the harvest. But on stevia I listen to the company man because he buys it.
